Which of a Term's Parameters Acts as an Intercept

Source: R/structural.R
term_level_param.Rd

Returns the name of the parameter, if any, that shifts the term's contribution by a constant and is therefore the same direction as an intercept in the equation in which the term sits.

Usage

term_level_param(term, ...)

Arguments

term

A term.

...

Passed to methods.

Value

A character vector: character(0) for a term that shifts nothing by a constant, "level1" for a regime, "omega" for an undeveloped gas() level, and otherwise the names of the level's coordinates whose design column is constant.

Details

It exists so that a fitting layer can resolve the confounding instead of rejecting the model. A score-driven level \(\omega\) and a regime's first level both add a constant to their equation's predictor: with an intercept there too, adding \(c\) to one and subtracting the matching amount from the other leaves every predictor unchanged, and the likelihood is flat along that direction. Which of the two is dropped is determined in the layer, because only the layer has the full list of terms in the equation.

The base method returns character(0), which means that the term does not shift its contribution by a constant and the question does not arise. The method for regime() returns "level1". The method for gas() returns "omega" when the level is not developed and otherwise every coordinate of the development whose design column is constant, which can be more than one.

See also

term_level_design() for the same question with the level developed, term_params() for the names from which the answer is taken.

Examples

term_level_param(gas(p = 1, q = 1))
#> [1] "omega"
term_level_param(regime(k = 2))
#> [1] "level1"
term_level_param(linpar(~x))
#> character(0)
